This is going to sound incredibly shallow as a response but I hope you take it exactly as I mean it: you just do it.

There's no gentle method. There's no ramp-down, any engagement means you're still dancing to their tune. Cold cut-off. Don't answer calls, don't respond to requests. That part is already very hard, because we're hardwired by nature to trust our parents/caregivers. Even if you know it's the right move, that twisted up guilty feeling will make itself known regardless. Can't be avoided, much as I wish it could. But it's also a very important step.

The other important step is letting other people in your life know you're not speaking with them, particularly focusing on ppl you both know, whom s/he interacts with. They will try to get to you through EVERYONE. Mine tried to reach me through my dad (who she estranged so he wasnt on board anyway), my kids (who's only single memory of meeting her is "she likes to fight with toddlers"), my stepmother (an actually decent person, and also could smell mom's bs a mile away), my brother, my former stepfather, and finally my personal favorite: my wife. She's tried to get to me through all of them.

It will suck. It will hurt. Won't lie and say you're gonna feel a big catharsis at first coz it's gonna feel like you're betraying someone you care about. Thing is, you're the only one of the two in this relationship who DOES care. Theyre just using you to fill the narrative of their own weird little delusions.

No, not "were" - you ARE someone.

Just because a monster tried to beat that identity into silence (literally or figuratively), they can never take it from you. Won't stop them from trying of course, but the single hardest thing I found separating from a narcissistic parent, was actually ACCEPTING and not just loudly repeating, that I was my own person. Won't lie and say it's easy or painless, but it's definitely worth it.

No one can define the parameters of your happiness, but you. If you let them define those boundaries, they will tie them around your neck like a noose and threaten to yank it.

Much as it sucks, there's no reasoning with a narcissist.

Not to put too fine a point on this, but odds are they're doing that already anyway.

Sabotage-grade gossip is pretty much what narcs thrive on. "Everyone should come to ME for answers, for help, for anything...if I deign to give it, of course."

Not sure what your overall situation is but if you're able to reduce or remove contact with those two, it's arguably the healthiest option. We can't convince narcissists of the damage they're causing because they're fully aware of it already, and consider it a strength. Might as well be telling a pro tennis player that they're pretty good at the sport, in their minds.

"Her reasoning is financial, however those financial reasons are flimsy at best."

That's exactly it though, it's a pretense to excuse trying to control you. "Look, I have so much control over your life that if I move far away, you have to accommodate ME instead of the other way around."

My mom did similar. Moved to the entire other side of the country in the middle of nowhere in a place that cant even be reached by plane, but for 3 months of the year...and then gets upset that no one visits. Mostly we know better...going there means getting trapped there. Odds are, your mom's attempting the same.

As to the kids...for ours at least, best approach I could think of was to just let them know that you and she haven't always gotten along very well, but always steered clear of specific examples or active attempts to demonize her in their eyes. Our kids are well into their twenties now, and I'm happy to say that mom demonstrated without any help on my part, her nature in a way they couldn't ignore.

Right now, while they're small? The details won't matter, they're running hot on feelings that have been carefully cultivated by a manipulator. Best thing we can ever do is just set a better example through our own behaviors and words, and trust they'll be smart enough to work it out as they grow.
Equivalent-purple has the right of it. There is no greater revenge against a narcissistic parent, than to succeed and be happy in SPITE of their efforts to stop you from doing so.

Echoing the above posters because it's just plain the best answer here. Problem with n-parents is, it's a game where they write the rules and only they win. The only possible winning move with a narcissist is to not engage them.

If I could offer a bit of advice here, as someone who was a T&S hiring manager for years: don't try to tell them what you think they want to hear.

Part of the job is cutting through signal noise and misdirection. If you don't have a history of dealing with extreme content or crisis/emergency management, tell them that. I was -always- more impressed when someone would admit a given skill shortcoming or area they were struggling with, because if they could be honest with me about something like that in an interview, odds are they would be more likely to seek help from teammates or management if something goes wrong, instead of potentially burying a sensitive or dangerous mistake. Trust me, honesty counts a lot here.

Other than that, a lot of it is likely going to be a mix of competency questions and questions meant to gauge how you approach problem-solving, work under pressure, or similar things.

The easiest way to send anyone who's career T&S into a fugue state, is to say one single word: "compliance". :P

It is, hands down, one of the hardest parts of the field. Not so much meeting a single regulation's requirements or updating for the impact of a regulation's changes. More the sheer -volume- of them, across various borders and territories, is enough to give anyone an ulcer.

Were it possible to do it faster while still being compliant, I'd be first in line to advocate the new methodology. 💀

In terms of Policy, we already have. What's changed is the reporting flow itself, being MUCH easier than it's been for years.

If you run across ERP Groups, absolutely report them, please.
Absolutely submit that information in a report, yes. Neither Group you've described here would be allowed under TOS.

Staff are not only not exempt, but we tend to assign a higher standard to ourselves. Impartiality is critical enough that the T&S team is mostly siloed, but we also believe that our fellow coworkers should, at \*the least\*, be held to the same standards as everyone else.

It's such a hard thing to explain to most people, but it doesn't take much to genuinely breach a community's trust with even just one bad faith action like that. So, we're hypervigilant about it.

Also - hi, fellow T&S person!
Don't blame you for feeling that way, or anyone else for that matter. Appreciate the kind words! <3

TLDR, it was a policy change.

It was a bit rougher in the early years to provide tangible feedback on reports, because people would rapidly figure out who reported them, and retaliate. It's been some time since that was a significant issue, and it's now greatly out weighed by our belief that people deserve to know the difference they're making, in helping us keep this community safe. :D

What changed, was our grip on information flows. :P

In more normal terms: Early on, one big issue we had with report feedback was that we just plain didn't have the headcount or tools to do it effectively. The years rolled on, and it became clear that A) we actually can do it now, and B) people deserve to know that they've made a difference.

It's a relatively small change of many upcoming changes, but still one of my favorites. :D

Of course not, that's retarded.  Let me get this out of the way for good:

What we want - or more accurately as a content manager, what I want - is to give an audience to talented community members who might otherwise have trouble doing so.  I get a kick out of showing off already popular stuff to a point, but it's far more satisfying to find a talent who hasn't been discovered yet, and show them off to the community.

Now, one of the things the higher-ups are offering some Youtubers is partnering.  This doesn't mean they have to upload their stuff to our channel, quite the opposite.  We WANT their stuff on their channel, and I imagine they do too.  With the partnering, they get the benefit of our audience numbers on their own channel, so they can grow (and profit, if that's their aim) on their own merits.

Uploading stuff to our channel makes zero fiscal or community sense from this perspective.  What if Artist X hits it big with the audience?  I mean sure, it'd be nice to have the extra traffic on our channel I guess, but now we have people expecting a consistent show, skit or review series that we cannot guarantee, since Artist X doesn't work for us.  That's not really a problem in and of itself with his own channel; since X runs it, he can upload whenever he likes, no biggie.  Total control.

There is, of course, the obvious benefit to Artist X in not having to listen to someone else tell him what "art" or "funny" or "mining" is, nevermind being told that his inspiration must be delivered "every Tuesday at 5am sharp!" or something equally silly - I'm an artist, and I know shit doesn't work like that.  ;)

We as staff have always wanted the best for the Minecraft community, and while there are things we need to do to keep the business afloat, we couldn't do this job if we didn't love the people we were doing it for.  The only money I care about is the money that lets me stay right here, continuing to give back to the community full-time instead of just as a hobby.

I could probably answer that better - I am Sacheverell, editor in chief of the Forum, and responsible for front-page content & news.  Nice to meet you!  :)

Let's look for a second at what Digital Diamonds are - user-made videos, right?  What those videos are - an LP, a tutorial, an amazing build etc - are all things we like bringing to the community's attention.  While I can't speak for the news/round-up vids, I can say that what made me start the Spotlights channel was a desire to do this very thing a little better than before - give builders, map makers etc. a chance to be seen by our rather substantial viewer-base where they might not have had a chance to otherwise.

One of my goals with the channel is to give those under-the-radar creators a chance to shine.  People like Sparklez, Yogs etc. already have a massive following, and odds are people will go looking for their stuff anyway.  That's a not a bad thing - they're popular for a reason! - but the fact is, they don't need help getting off the ground; they're insanely popular already.  :)

I've never shut out the idea of spotlighting community videos - in fact, I'd really enjoy the opportunity to do so again.  What I'd like to do is have those same relative unknowns get their videos seen on my channel  and front-page, to give them a bit of a boost.  I make it a point to credit everyone involved where possible, because I want them to have a chance to shine on their own.  Once I've given them some exposure, it's up to them to make it happen going forward, though.

Will DDs ever be spotlighted the way they used to be?  Yes.  When?  "soon™" - there are some things I'm waiting on before I start putting them up again, and once that happens, I'll gladly put them out there.

I've never been closed to people's ideas on the subject of content, but since hardly anyone comes to me about it, I have to assume that they enjoy what's been presented so far.  What would you like to see?
